preamble: Voicing of the voiceless velar fricative [x] to [ɣ]. Under Verner's law, the Proto-Germanic *x that Grimm's law produced from Proto-Indo-European *k and *ḱ became *ɣ when the preceding vowel was unaccented, so that root-stressed and suffix-stressed forms of one root diverge: *teuhaną 'to pull' against *tugōną 'to tug', *swehuraz 'father-in-law' against *swegrō 'mother-in-law'. In Polish, /x/ has a voiced allophone [ɣ] before a voiced obstruent, also across a word boundary.

examples.from: Pre-Germanic *duk-éh₂-yo-nom 'lead' (accent on the suffix), with *k > *x by Grimm's law
examples.note: Wikipedia's Verner's law article pairs it with root-stressed Pre-Germanic *déwk-o-nom, which kept the voiceless fricative: *teuhaną /ˈteu̯.xɑ.nɑ̃/ 'to pull' (German ziehen, Old High German zogōn 'to tug, drag').

examples.from: PIE *sweḱrúh₂ 'mother-in-law' (accent on the suffix), with *ḱ > *x by Grimm's law

languageExamples.context: Before a voiced obstruent, also across a word boundary

examples.to: dach domu [daɣ ˈdɔmu] 'roof of the house'
examples.note: Word-final /x/ is voiced by the following /d/; Wikipedia gives the rule as applying even across a word boundary.
